fields.title: Ebola outbreak: MSF statement on WHO Director General’s high-level visit to DRC
fields.body:
**Dr Philippa Boulle, deputy medical director for Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), provides a statement on the occasion of Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus’, Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO), high-level visit to Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).**

“Two and a half months after the [Ebola disease outbreak](https://www.msf.org/drc-ebola-outbreaks) was declared, the situation in eastern [DRC](https://www.msf.org/democratic-republic-congo-drc) is more critical than ever. The [outbreak](https://www.msf.org/epidemics-and-pandemics) is spreading at an alarming and unprecedented rate, despite the tireless efforts of frontline medical teams.

According to the WHO, 3,605 confirmed cases had been reported by 1 August, making this the largest [Ebola](https://www.msf.org/ebola) outbreak ever recorded in the DRC, surpassing the 2018 epidemic. In just 11 weeks since it was declared, nearly 1,500 people have died. That is a far higher death toll than in comparable periods of previous outbreaks; the devastating 2014 Ebola outbreak in West Africa caused 279 deaths over the same timeframe.

Even more concerning, the outbreak shows no sign of slowing down. New suspected cases are being reported almost daily in new locations, outside already identified transmission chains. To prevent further loss of life, the response must outpace the current rate of transmission. The international medical response must scale-up without delay, and many critical gaps still need to be addressed.

Undeniable progress has been made in screening and contact tracing, but these efforts remain very insufficient to contain the epidemic. In the MSF Ebola treatment centre in Bunia, 90 per cent of admitted patients were not traced contacts, while in the whole of Ituri province only 59 per cent of contacts were traced. There is an urgent need for improved community engagement. A successful response can only be achieved if it is built with and led by local organisations. Without communities at the centre of the response, surveillance and contact tracing will continue to miss cases. Better integration of local communities is essential to ensure cases are detected as early as possible and followed up rigorously.

This outbreak is aggravating an ongoing humanitarian crisis. [Malaria](https://www.msf.org/malaria), [measles](https://www.msf.org/measles), [cholera](https://www.msf.org/cholera), [malnutrition](https://www.msf.org/malnutrition), and other preventable and treatable conditions continue to cause significant illness and death. Continued support for health facilities is also critical so they can keep providing vital healthcare services throughout the response and protect health workers.

Access remains a critical issue, particularly in remote areas where the onset of the rainy season will make movement difficult and risk disrupting operations. Providing medical supplies, as well as incentives and support for frontline health workers, is essential. Clear assurances are needed that border restrictions, sanitary measures, or administrative burdens will not impede humanitarian staff rotations, medical referrals, or the delivery of supplies. For now, the situation remains uncertain.

Strengthening epidemiological surveillance, improving community engagement, and guaranteeing access for humanitarian personnel are top priorities.

The response is expanding but is still not reaching communities quickly enough to break transmission chains. Immediate action is needed. Every day lost allows the virus to stay one step ahead and more lives to be needlessly lost.”

fields.title: Bulletin d’information : Accès aux marchés, préférences d’assistance et faisabilité des interventions cash auprès des personnes déplacées à Nyemba (Juin 2026)
fields.body:
**Contexte**

À la suite d’une escalade des affrontements armés dans le territoire d’Uvira en décembre 2025, des milliers de personnes ont été déplacées. Près de 40 000 personnes déplacées internes (PDI) ont trouvé refuge dans la zone de santé de Nyemba, dans la province du Tanganyika, dont environ 30 000 réparties dans 11 nouveaux sites spontanés. Cet afflux massif de population a accru la pression sur les services de base et les marchés locaux, tout en générant d’importants besoins humanitaires.

Dans ce contexte, une analyse des dynamiques de marché dans la zone de santé de Nyemba est essentielle afin d’évaluer la faisabilité des interventions en transferts monétaires, d’identifier les risques potentiels associés à leur mise en oeuvre et d’orienter le choix des modalités d’assistance les plus adaptées.

Les transferts monétaires constituent une option de réponse susceptible de répondre aux besoins des ménages déplacés tout en soutenant les marchés locaux. Toutefois, leur mise en oeuvre nécessite une compréhension approfondie du fonctionnement des marchés et de leur capacité à absorber une augmentation de la demande. L’arrivée rapide d’un grand nombre de ménages déplacés peut en effet entraîner une hausse de la demande en biens alimentaires et non alimentaires, susceptible d’exercer des pressions inflationnistes si l’offre locale ne s’ajuste pas suffisamment. En outre, d’éventuels déséquilibres entre l’offre et la demande pourraient réduire l’accessibilité économique des biens essentiels pour les populations les plus vulnérables et accentuer les tensions sociales liées aux disparités de pouvoir d’achat.

fields.title: Cameroon Education Cluster: Quarter | Operational Presence and Realization (Jan-Mar 2026)
fields.body:
The NWSW Education Cluster initially determined that **505,170** persons within the education sphere in the NWSW need education related supported in the North West and South West Regions. Also, the cluster targeted **347,585** persons (**342,004** children and **5,580** teachers and education staff). During the reprioritization, the targets were refocused on the most affected Divisions in severity 4 using the JIAF 2. methodology. This gave us **190,119** persons. that is **187,120** children and **2,999** teachers to be reached in 2026.

From January to March 2026, **16** Education cluster partners implemented activities in 12 out of 13 Divisions of the NWSW, with the exception of Momo Division in the North West due to the lack of partners presence. These activities were funded by through 19 organization including 9 external funders **(European Union, Education Cannot Wait (ECW), UNICEF, SIDA, Stone Family Foundation (SFF), UNESCO, Building Schools for Africa, GOETHE INSTITUT, Leading Well Network).** Six (6) national organizations also funded some of their activities.

A total of **70,089** persons including **70,071 (99.9%)** children and **18** teachers and education related persons) were reached. A total of **2,604 (4%)** persons with disabilities were reached with **428** being persons with disabilities reached for the first time during the year.

The overall reach of **70,089 persons** (**37%**) of the reprioritized target of **190,119**. The reprioritized Divisions for the 2026 PiN and Targets included*: Donga-Mantung, Menchum, Mezam, Momo, Ngo-Ketunjia, Lebialem, and Ndian.* However, the above results encompass results from other divisions not prioritized in the 2026 targets. **67%** of the results were reported from the South West while **31%** were reported from the North West. Mezam is the Division with the most reach, followed by Donga-Mantung, and Bui Divisions. The least 3 were Meme, Ndian, Kupe-Mounengumba Divisions. Non-formal education was not implemented in Momo Division.

From the total number of persons reached, **100%** were reached through non-formal education channels, such as Temporary Learning Spaces (TLS), and community schools.

Out of the **70,089,** persons reached, **56%** were females, while **44%** were males. A total of **11,170** persons reached for the first time from January to March 2026 out of which **36% (3,992)** were host community members who had never been displaced, **16% (1,768)** were returnees (i.e. host community members who were displaced and have returned to their primary community of residence, and **48%(5,410)** were people still living under internal displacement status. This is also comprised of **67% (7,528)** girls, **32% (3,624)** boys, and **1% (18)** adults (who are teachers and school management committee members).

The top 3 activities implemented were (*1*) the implementation of Radio Education Programmes & digital learning platforms, which reached **70,071 (99.97%)** children reached with **39,691 (57%)** girls, **30,380 (43%)** boys. (*2*) The implementation of recreational activities (psychosocial activities) for children in schools and temporary learning spaces reached **11,357 (16%)** persons (**9,199** children and **2,158** teachers). Amongst the children were **5,696 (50%)** girls and **3,503(31%)** boys. (*3*) A total of **440 (0.63%)** children were reached with the provision of inclusive and accessible formal education to children affected by the crisis in the North West and South West Regions.

**Attacks on Education:** A total of **8** attacks were reported from January to March 2026, after triangulation by education cluster partners from the North West and South West Regions. **75% (6)** of the attacks were reported from the NW, while **25% (2)** were reported from the SW. Allegedly, all **8** attacks were kidnappings and arbitrary arrests. A total of **25** persons were allegedly affected by these attacks.

fields.title: RD Congo : Situation humanitaire dans la province du Sud-Kivu – rapport de situation #7, 24 juillet 2026
fields.body:
**Faits majeurs**

Des affrontements armés se sont intensifiés dans les hauts plateaux de Fizi et Mwenga provoquant des nouveaux déplacements de population, l’accroissement des besoins et davantage des contraintes d’accès humanitaire.  
 Près de 60 000 personnes bénéficient d’un appui à la production agricole d'urgence dans la zone de santé de Minova, en territoire de Kalehe.

**CHIFFRES CLÉS**

1,01 million de personnes déplacées internes au 30 juin 2026

1,16 million de personnes retournées au 30 juin 2026

600 000 personnes ont bénéficié d’un appui à la production agricole d’urgence dans le territoire de Kalehe

**APERÇU DE LA SITUATION**

**Territoire de Fizi**  
 En juin 2026, les affrontements se sont intensifiés sur les Hauts Plateaux du territoire de Fizi, notamment dans la zone de santé (ZS) de Minembwe. Selon des sources locales, les combats ont fait des victimes civiles, détruit des infrastructures essentielles et provoqué de nouveaux déplacements. Le 10 juin, La ZS de Nundu a également accueilli plus de 8 500 personnes ayant fui les violences dans les villages de Mikenge et Bilamboli dans le territoire de Mwenga. La détérioration de la sécurité a fortement restreint l’accès humanitaire, privant durablement les populations déplacées, retournées et hôtes de services essentiels. Les prix des denrées alimentaires déjà intenables ont continué à flamber, aggravant la vulnérabilité de la population.  
**Territoire de Kalehe**  
 Les combats incessants sur les Hauts Plateaux de Ziralo ont provoqué le déplacement de plus de 43 800 personnes vers les ZS de Kalehe et de Minova au cours du mois de juin 2026, selon des alertes humanitaires. Ces nouveaux arrivants ont considérablement aggravé des besoins humanitaires déjà critiques sur place.  
**Territoire Mwenga**  
 En juin, des combats se sont intensifiés dans les Hauts Plateaux d’Itombwe, notamment à Mikenge et dans les localités de Ntondo, Lurhala, Kashadu et Kasihe. Le 21 et le 22 juin, des violences armées ont causé des pertes civiles, détruit des infrastructures et des habitations, et entraîné le déplacement de plus de 3 100 personnes vers plusieurs villages de la ZS de Mwana dont Kakwende et Mulambi, selon des sources locales. La dégradation sécuritaire a également fortement limité l’accès humanitaire dans plusieurs zones à forts besoins humanitaires.

fields.title: Afrique de l’Ouest et centrale : Derniers événements en bref (du 28 juillet au 3 août 2026)
fields.body:
**République démocratique du Congo** 

**La violence, les déplacements de population et** **Ebola aggravent la crise humanitaire** 

Des rapports indiquent que la poursuite des combats dans les hautes terres de la province du Sud-Kivu contraint les populations à fuir leurs foyers et perturbe l’accès aux services essentiels. Selon les partenaires humanitaires, les affrontements dans les territoires d’Uvira, de Fizi et de Mwenga ont provoqué le déplacement de plus de 48 000 personnes depuis la mi-juillet. Des victimes civiles et des dégâts aux infrastructures essentielles ont également été signalés. 

OCHA attire l'attention sur le fait que l'insécurité, les fermetures de routes, les infrastructures endommagées et les coupures de télécommunications entravent gravement l'accès humanitaire, les évacuations médicales et l'acheminement de l'aide vitale. 

Les services de santé ont été particulièrement touchés. Les dégâts subis par les établissements de santé et le départ du personnel médical ont réduit l'accès aux soins, privant ainsi plus de 80 personnes blessées par la violence armée et les restes explosifs de guerre des traitements dont elles auraient besoin depuis le début de l'année. Par ailleurs, les efforts de lutte contre Ebola se poursuivent au Sud-Kivu, où les autorités sanitaires surveillent 55 personnes identifiées comme ayant été en contact avec des cas confirmés. Au 1er août, les autorités nationales avaient signalé 3 748 cas confirmés d’Ebola dans les provinces de l’Ituri, du Nord- Kivu, du Sud-Kivu, du Haut-Uele et du Tshopo.  
OCHA réitère son appel à toutes les parties pour qu’elles protègent les civils, garantissent un accès humanitaire sûr et durable, et rétablissent les télécommunications, qui sont essentielles à la protection des civils, aux efforts de santé publique et aux opérations humanitaires.

**Ghana** 

**La CEDEAO alloue 250 000 dollars américains pour** **faire face aux inondations** 

La Communauté économique des États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (CEDEAO) a annoncé une contribution de 250 000 US$ destinée à soutenir les opérations de secours en faveur des personnes affectées par les inondations survenues fin juin au Ghana. Ces inondations, provoquées par de fortes pluies, ont fait au moins 12 morts et touché environ 38 800 habitants répartis dans 7 761 foyers de la région du Grand Accra. 

Ce financement est destiné à soutenir les opérations humanitaires en cours, notamment la mise à disposition d'abris d'urgence, de nourriture et de produits de première nécessité. Les opérations d'intervention et de reconstruction se poursuivent dans les communautés les plus touchées, et une aide supplémentaire est apportée à certaines parties de la région de la Volta où des dégâts ont également été signalés au niveau des habitations et des infrastructures.

**Congo** 

**Republic of the Congo steps up Ebola** **preparedness** 

Les autorités ont renforcé les contrôles sanitaires à la plage de Brazzaville, à l'aéroport international de Maya-Maya et à d'autres points d'entrée à la suite de l'épidémie d'Ebola qui sévit en RD Congo voisine. Le risque de transmission transfrontalière étant jugé élevé, les autorités sanitaires ont renforcé les systèmes de surveillance, d'isolement et d'orientation vers des structures spécialisées, formé le personnel de première ligne et intensifié les actions de sensibilisation au sein de la population. 

L'OMS et ses partenaires ont également acheminé plus de 25 tonnes de médicaments et de matériel médical d'une valeur d'environ 280 000 US$.

fields.title: West and Central Africa: Latest Events at a glance (28 July–3 August 2026)
fields.body:
**Democratic Republic of the Congo**

**Violence, displacement and Ebola compound humanitarian crisis**

Reports highlight that continued fighting in the highlands of South Kivu Province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is forcing people to flee their homes and disrupting access to essential services. According to humanitarian partners, clashes in the territories of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga have displaced more than 48,000 people since mid-July.  
Civilian casualties and damage to critical infrastructure have also been reported.

OCHA warns that insecurity, road closures, damaged infrastructure and telecommunications outages are severely constraining humanitarian access, medical evacuations and the delivery of life-saving assistance. Healthcare services have been particularly affected. Damage to health facilities and the departure of medical staff have reduced access to medical care, leaving more than 80 people injured by armed violence and explosive remnants of war without the treatment they reportedly need since the start of the year.  
Meanwhile, Ebola response efforts continue in South Kivu, where health authorities are monitoring 55 people identified as contacts of confirmed cases. As of 1 August, national authorities had reported 3,748 confirmed Ebola cases across Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele and Tshopo provinces.

OCHA reiterates its call on all parties to protect civilians, ensure safe and sustained humanitarian access, and restore telecommunications, which are vital for civilian protection, public health efforts and humanitarian operations.

**Ghana**

**ECOWAS allocates US$250,000 for flood response**

The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) has announced a US$250,000 contribution to support relief efforts for people affected by the late-June floods in Ghana. The floods, triggered by heavy rainfall, left at least 12 people dead and impacted approximately 38,800 residents across 7,761 households in the Greater Accra Region.

The funding is intended to assist ongoing humanitarian response activities, including the provision of emergency shelter, food, and essential supplies. Response and recovery operations are still underway in the worst-affected communities, with additional support being extended to parts of the Volta Region where damage to homes and infrastructure has also been reported.

**Congo**

**Republic of the Congo steps up Ebola preparedness**

Authorities have strengthened health screening at Brazzaville Beach, Maya-Maya International Airport and other entry points following the Ebola outbreak in neighbouring DRC. With the risk of cross-border transmission assessed as high, health authorities have reinforced surveillance, isolation and referral systems, trained frontline staff and expanded community awareness.  
The World Health Organization and partners have also delivered more than 25 tonnes of medicines and medical supplies worth about US$280,000.

fields.title: Cameroon Cholera Outbreak: Situation Report #2 (August 4, 2026)
fields.body:
**FAST FACTS**

- As of August 2, 53 suspected cholera cases had been reported in Minawao Refugee Camp, which hosts 81,022 refugees and is operating at 324% of its intended capacity, creating conditions conducive to rapid disease transmission.
- Multiple transmission chains are suspected within the camp, increasing the risk of further spread among vulnerable refugee and host populations.
- As of August 2, the cholera outbreak in the Far North Region had resulted in 990 reported cases and 28 deaths across nine affected health districts.

**OUR RESPONSE**

- International Medical Corps is coordinating with health authorities, UN agencies, camp management and humanitarian partners to support a harmonized response.
- We are implementing cholera prevention and response activities focused on outbreak containment, case management and community protection.
- Efforts include strengthening treatment capacity through additional staff, essential medicines and cholera supplies, and strengthening surveillance, community alert systems and risk communication to support early detection and treatment.
- We also are scaling up risk communication, hygiene promotion, infection prevention, disinfection, and emergency activities involving water, sanitation and hygiene.

Following the detection of suspected and RDT-positive cholera cases in Minawao Refugee Camp, International Medical Corps launched an emergency response to support outbreak containment and reduce cholera-related morbidity and mortality among refugee and host communities. Implemented in coordination with national authorities and humanitarian partners, our intervention addresses critical operational gaps and is expected to directly benefit more than 14,500 people through enhanced surveillance, case management, infection prevention and control, risk communication and community engagement, and water, sanitation and hygiene interventions.

Patients suspected to have cholera have received direct clinical care from International Medical Corps teams in the temporary treatment unit that we have set up in the main section of the Minawao Medicalized Health Center, located inside the camp. This care continues while efforts to expand treatment capacity remain underway. We so far have managed 53 patients, including 26 discharged as recovered, with no deaths reported to date, while we have identified and monitored 217 contacts. The Mokolo Health District has led efforts to conduct rapid investigations, contact tracing, active case finding, household disinfection and refer suspected cases for higher care, while International Medical Corps has strengthened response readiness through training on cholera case management and diagnostics. We also have supported treatment and IPC activities by providing contingency stocks and mobilizing additional personnel, medicines, consumables and response supplies.

fields.title: CPAoR GBV Safety Audits for Children Key Findings (NW/SW Cameroon, 2025)
fields.body:
## Executive Summary

The **GBV Safety Audit (North-West and South-West Cameroon, 2025)** assessed gender-based violence (GBV) risks affecting children, particularly adolescent girls, across 64 crisis-affected communities. Using **719 key informant interviews, 500 focus group discussions involving 5,602 participants, 207 safety walks, and mapping of 103 service providers**, the assessment identified widespread protection risks, major service gaps, and priority actions for humanitarian actors.

The audit found that **physical violence (22.1%), sexual violence (20.4%), rape (18.4%), and psychological abuse (16.2%)** are among the most prevalent forms of GBV. High-risk locations include bushes, farms, water points, roads, markets, and household surroundings, while insecurity is driven by the presence of armed groups, poor lighting, isolation, youth gangs, and limited trusted security services. Inadequate infrastructure further increases risks, with many communities lacking safe water points, gender-segregated latrines, lighting, and privacy. Schools also present significant protection concerns, including unsafe access routes, harassment, transactional sex for grades, and inadequate menstrual hygiene facilities.

The assessment also highlights critical barriers to protection and survivor support. GBV services remain limited and unevenly distributed, with insufficient availability of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) kits, low awareness of referral mechanisms, and a severe shortage of Women and Girls Safe Spaces. As a result, survivors often rely on informal community structures rather than specialized services.

To address these challenges, the report recommends a coordinated, multi-sectoral response focused on strengthening prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), expanding safe and accessible WASH infrastructure, improving child safeguarding in schools, ensuring survivor-centred health services, strengthening case management and referral systems, and promoting community engagement to reduce harmful practices and GBV risks. Overall, the audit concludes that sustained collaboration across child protection, GBV, health, WASH, education, and general protection sectors is essential to reduce GBV risks and improve access to quality services for affected children and communities.

fields.body:
## Résumé de la situation

La province de l'Ituri demeure l'épicentre de l'épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola (MVE) en RDC. Au 27 juillet 2026, 2 988 cas confirmés et 1 238 décès avaient été enregistrés dans 28 des 36 zones de santé de la province. La transmission communautaire reste active et continue de s'étendre dans plusieurs zones de santé.

Les sites et centres collectifs situés dans les zones affectées présentent des facteurs susceptibles d'accroître le risque de transmission, notamment la forte densité de population, la promiscuité, les insuffisances en eau, hygiène et assainissement (WASH), ainsi que les mouvements fréquents entre les sites, les communautés d'accueil et les marchés. Dans ce contexte, le renforcement de la surveillance communautaire, de la coordination intersectorielle et des mesures de prévention demeure essentiel pour limiter les risques dans les sites.
